patches.proposed_text: In the tested native formulation, the reference-centered triplet is treated as a whole-expression relation. Its reference, orientation roles, and distinction capacity may be named as OTM-exposed aspects, but the present finite constructions do not establish them as independently realizable complete relations.

Equality of a tested observed slice or closed result should not by itself be used as a sufficient identity test for the pre-closure whole relation; the conclusion is limited to the declared predicates and constructions.

The tested perturbation campaign identifies symmetry reference, orientation roles, and distinction capacity as a candidate identity basis for this modeled triplet. This is a bounded candidate result, not a proof of universal minimality.

OTM should be described here as an admissible reconstruction surface in the tested model. The supplied evidence does not establish that an OTM output is the historical pre-closure triplet or that all lawful decompositions are generated.

In the tested constructions, different pre-closure organizations can map to the same closed result. This is recorded as a possible representation-level loss of historical signature, not as a universal property of every MTO realization.
limitations: Closure map and model class are bounded

patches.proposed_text: Whether a phase signature is recoverable after closure remains an open research question. FAT-24 tested one mapping in which pre-closure signatures were not preserved; that result does not settle recoverability for other mappings.
The tested evidence treats distinction capacity as a whole-relation condition that can be exposed as an aspect, while its independent realization remains unsupported in the tested domain.
